description: We are a team of software engineering and data science students from Sri Lanka, passionate about building real-world tech solutions.
summary: The Abandoned Explorers is an interactive 3D web experience for children aged 8 to 14. It takes them from Home on Earth at night, through a rocket launch, to the Moon or Mars, where they meet the machines NASA left behind: rovers, landers, a helicopter and a probe. Each machine tells its own mission story in the first person, and the child plays that mission. Driving a rover with a signal delay, catching a seismic tremor, timing a radio echo or managing a lander's power are real mission problems turned into short games. Each child can also ask a machine questions in a chat that answers only from that mission's checked NASA facts, always with the source. The experience works in English, Sinhala and Tamil. It answers the challenge by showing what discarded equipment did, what it found, and why it is still worth remembering.

▸ What if the machines could talk?

Twelve machines in our app are still out there: eight on Mars, four on the Moon. Rovers, landers, a helicopter, science stations. They measured marsquakes, found signs of ancient water and drove further than anyone expected. Then they went quiet. The Abandoned Explorers gives them their voices back, so a child can meet them, play their missions, and ask them questions.

Caption: Every journey starts at home, on a launch pad under a real night sky.Caption: The project in numbers, counted from our code and data.

▸ Your mission starts at home

The child boards a rocket, lifts off, and chooses a world. They land among the real machines, each standing on its own plinth: a memorial for the silent ones. Pointing at a machine opens a hologram with its real landing site, its years of service, a key fact and the NASA page it came from.

Caption: The whole journey, from Earth to a machine's story.Caption: Choose your world.Caption: The explorers of Mars, each with its years of service.Caption: Opportunity drove 45.16 km and last spoke to Earth on 10 June 2018.Caption: 57 years of explorers, from Surveyor 3 (1967) to Ingenuity (2024).

▸ Don't read about it. Do it.

Each machine tells its own story in the first person. Then the child does what the real mission team did: plan Sojourner's path around rocks, hold steady to scan a rock, catch a marsquake on a seismograph, keep a lander alive with limited power, and race the plan against what really happened. Real mission numbers become game numbers. Every game has a clear goal, a hint, instant feedback, a funny fail with instant retry, a Skip button and a win moment.

Caption: Plan Sojourner's route and stay clear of the rocks.Caption: 37 mini-games across 11 stories. Zero quizzes.

▸ Ask a machine anything

"What did you discover?" Sojourner answers in its own voice, using only checked NASA facts, and links each answer to its source. A server check rejects any number that is not in the facts. With no internet, the app still answers by choosing the best checked fact.

Caption: Sojourner explains its discoveries, with a link to the source.

▸ If it isn't on a NASA page, it isn't in the game

Every one of our 207 facts is stored with the NASA page it came from: 28 pages from the challenge resources and the NASA pages named in our story briefs. Anything we could not confirm is marked TODO-VERIFY, never guessed. An automatic fact checker runs before every deploy. The AI chat is held to the same facts.

Caption: The path every fact takes before a child sees or hears it.

▸ Turn it, tap it, learn it

NASA's own 3D models can be turned around. Tap a numbered part to see what it did and what we learned from it.

Caption: InSight's RISE radio, and what it revealed about Mars's core.

▸ Under the hood

A cinematic 3D world that runs in any browser: no install, no app store, no account. TypeScript, Vite and three.js, with GSAP cutscenes, particle effects, and music and sound made live with Web Audio. Voices come from Kokoro-82M. The chat runs Gemini on Google Cloud Run, and its key never reaches the browser. Hosted on Firebase and deployed by GitHub Actions after linting, 43 automated tests and the fact check. Everything runs on free tiers and Space Apps Global Offers.

Caption: The technology, layer by layer.Caption: How the browser, the build and the chat server fit together.

▸ For every child, in their own language

English, Sinhala and Tamil, with 1,208 lines of text in each. Every cutscene can be skipped, every control works with keyboard and touch, and motion is reduced when the device asks for it.

▸ Why it matters

Children learn that "abandoned" does not mean "forgotten". These machines found signs of water, measured marsquakes and drove marathons, and their data is still used today. Play makes the science stick, and the chat lets curiosity lead.

▸ Honest limits and next missions

  • Tamil text is waiting for review by native speakers.
  • The Home opening film is AI-generated and labelled as such.
  • Next: more stories.
